pr.title: Allow more MIR SROA
pr.description:
This removes some guards on SROA that are no longer needed:
- With https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/838 it no longer needs to check for SIMD
- With https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/807 it no longer needs to check for niches
  - This means that `Wrapper(char)` and `Pin<&mut T>` can get SRoA'd now, where previously they weren't because the check was banning SRaA for anything with a niche -- not just things with `#[rustc_layout_scalar_valid_range_*]`.
  - Technically rust-lang/rust#133652 isn't complete yet, but `NonZero` and `NonNull` have already moved over, so this is fine.  At worst this will mean that LLVM gets less `!range` metadata on something that wasn't already fixed by rust-lang/rust#133651 or rust-lang/rust#135236, but that's still sound, and unblocking general SRoA is worth that tradeoff.
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR (rust-lang/rust#144543) does not describe a semantically incorrect rewrite. It only widens SROA's eligibility: the old `escaping_locals` conservatively refused to flatten single-field, niche-bearing ADTs such as `Wrapper(char)` and `Pin<&mut T>`, while the new code allows flattening them. The provided MIR diff confirms the change is representational: old MIR constructs `Pin { pointer: copy _45 }` and immediately kills it, while new MIR directly forms `&mut (_19.0)`; subsequent accesses still use the same underlying field (`(*_45).0` versus `(*_19.0).0`). The PR text explicitly states this is still sound and only may reduce LLVM `!range` metadata. Thus any pair of Rust functions modeling "keep the aggregate local" versus "scalar-replace the aggregate local" must produce identical observable values on all defined inputs. Producing different original/transformed outputs would require adding an unrelated change (e.g. mutating or reading a different value between aggregate construction and field access), which is prohibited. There is therefore no source-grounded concrete counterexample to validate with test_program_pair.

analysis.summary: SROA's escaping-locals filter was widened by removing the `#[repr(simd)]` guard and the broad "any ADT with a niche escapes" guard. Only unions/enums and the DynMetadata lang item remain unconditionally excluded, so single-field niche-bearing wrappers such as `Wrapper(char)` and `Pin<&mut T>` can now be scalar-replaced.
analysis.originalLogic: In `escaping_locals`, a local was treated as escaping if its type was a union or enum; if its type was an ADT, it was also excluded when `def.repr().simd()`, when it was the `DynMetadata` lang item, or when `layout.layout.largest_niche().is_some()`. The last check applied to any ADT with a niche, not just scalar-valid-range types. ADTs with more than one field explicitly returned false so only single-field wrappers were affected by the niche check. The pass then used this escaping set to decide which locals could be flattened by `compute_flattening`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, for a single-field, non-union, non-enum ADT with a layout niche but no `#[rustc_layout_scalar_valid_range_*]` (for example `Pin<&mut T>` or a custom `Wrapper(char)`), the pass marked the local as escaping and therefore did not decompose it. Aggregate construction and field access remained on the whole wrapper, as in the old MIR diff line `_47 = Pin::<&mut std::future::Ready<()>> { pointer: copy _45 };`. The corrected transformation lets such a local proceed to flattening, so the wrapper aggregate is no longer constructed and its field is accessed directly, as in `_47 = &mut (_19.0: &mut std::future::Ready<()>);`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing candidate locals whose type is a non-union, non-enum ADT that has a niche, especially single-field wrappers such as `Pin<&mut T>`, `Wrapper(char)`, or other niche-carrying newtypes. The supplied regression context exposes such a local after inlining `Pin::as_mut`/`DerefMut` in a coroutine body. SIMD ADTs are the other removed guard category. Unions, enums, and `DynMetadata<T>` remain outside this widening.
analysis.trigger: A local of an ADT type is considered by SROA's escaping analysis; under the old guard the local escapes merely because its layout has a niche (or because it is `repr(simd)`). After the change, only unions/enums and `DynMetadata` are excluded by these checks, so the niche-bearing wrapper reaches `compute_flattening`.
preconditions: The local's type must not be a union or enum.
The local's ADT must not be the `DynMetadata` lang item; that exclusion is retained.
Under the historical logic, the ADT must have `largest_niche().is_some()` for the extra exclusion to fire; a niche is necessary for the old behavior being removed.
The ADT should be a single-field wrapper for the old `variant.fields.len() > 1` early-return not to bypass the niche check.
The regression context is MIR after inlining has introduced/retained a `Pin<&mut T>` local, but the modified analysis itself is SROA.
pitfalls: Do not attribute the changed behavior to the Inline pass because the retained test is named `inline_coroutine_body...Inline...`; the source change is in `sroa.rs` and the diff shows the Pin aggregate disappearing after SROA.
The niche guard was broader than intended: it also excluded types without `#[rustc_layout_scalar_valid_range_*]`, which is exactly why `Wrapper(char)` and `Pin<&mut T>` were previously blocked.
The PR description warns that LLVM may get less `!range` metadata for something not already fixed elsewhere, but states `that's still sound`; do not infer unsoundness from the removed guard alone.
The retained `DynMetadata` exclusion has a codegen reason: `codegen wants to see the `DynMetadata<T>`,` and `not the inner reference-to-opaque-type.`
SIMD guard removal is justified by external compiler-team work, not by the local code alone: `With https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/838 it no longer needs to check for SIMD`.
The new MIR still performs the same field accesses, e.g. `_47 = &mut (_19.0: &mut std::future::Ready<()>);`; SROA changes representation, not the underlying borrow/access semantics.
Local renumbering and removal of `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` for the eliminated wrapper in the decoded diff are consequences of flattening, not separate optimizations.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a mir-opt test (the supplied patch updates `tests/mir-opt/inline_coroutine_body.run2-{closure#0}.Inline.panic-abort.diff` and `...panic-unwind.diff`) that exposes a `Pin<&mut T>`-like local after inlining and dumps MIR after SROA. Compare old vs new guard behavior: with the old niche guard the wrapper aggregate should remain visible (e.g. `Pin::<...> { pointer: copy ... }`); with the new guard it should be absent while direct field accesses remain. Add focused negative/coverage cases for `DynMetadata` (must still remain aggregate), enum/union (still excluded), and a `repr(simd)` candidate for the removed SIMD guard. Do not claim runtime reproduction; this is a MIR-diff regression test, and no compiler was built here.

With https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/838 it no longer needs to check for SIMD

This means that `Wrapper(char)` and `Pin<&mut T>` can get SRoA'd now, where previously they weren't because the check was banning SRaA for anything with a niche -- not just things with `#[rustc_layout_scalar_valid_range_*]`.

At worst this will mean that LLVM gets less `!range` metadata on something that wasn't already fixed by rust-lang/rust#133651 or rust-lang/rust#135236, but that's still sound, and unblocking general SRoA is worth that tradeoff.
